assumptions: Without the change, all units move in parallel
A unit does not stop the change after it starts
avoid_when: The units got the change at different times and the effect is different for each group (the result can be wrong)
You want to forecast (the time effects are only for the periods of the data)
data_needs: The same number for each unit over time

about.example: A new store layout in 12 of 30 stores added 5% to monthly sales, and the stores moved together before the change.
about.expert_notes: Bayesian two-way fixed effects: unit and time effects (ZeroSumNormal; time effects iid or a random walk) plus event-time dummies (reference period -1, endpoints binned at -leads/+lags) or one treatment dummy (design 'did'). Under staggered adoption with effects that differ between cohorts, TWFE estimates can be biased (Goodman-Bacon 2021, Sun and Abraham 2021): the model emits a STAGGERED_ADOPTION warning. Counterfactual mode sets treatment to 0.
outputs: The average effect of the change with a range
The effect for each period before and after the change
A warning when the units got the change at different times

references.title: Goodman-Bacon (2021), Difference-in-differences with variation in treatment timing, Journal of Econometrics
Sun and Abraham (2021), Estimating dynamic treatment effects in event studies with heterogeneous treatment effects, Journal of Econometrics

about.summary_plain: Measures the effect of a change that some stores or markets got and others did not. It shows the effect for each period before and after the change.
about.title: Before and after, with a comparison group
use_when: Some units got a change and other units never got it
The units got the change at the same time or at different times
You want to see if the groups moved the same way before the change
